messages:
jess (support): heads-up — Morphix hitting 429s on /v1/complete around the top of the minute. Their dashboard shows avg RPM ~1450 (account limit 1500) but they see short spikes that result in 429s. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/MORPH-915

morphix-support: Confirming — spikes are very short, ~150–250 reqs in a 2–4s window, looks like bursty clients. No deploys or config changes on our side.

ops-bot: Alert: rate-limit breach detected for acct=morphix at 2024-07-21T03:12:01Z. sample headers observed: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 1500`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 169`, 429 count +22 in last minute.

samir (devex): can you paste one raw response headers payload and your client stack? SDK or custom? Also are they all coming from the same IPs (proxy) or many ephemeral IPs?

morphix-support: sample response headers we captured:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1500
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 12
X-Request-Id: req_01Gx...
Content-Type: application/json
```

Clients: internal microservices using our in-house SDK (node 16). They run hundreds of short-lived lambda-style containers behind a NAT gateway (so same public IP).

maria (sre): probable cause: minute-window RPM bucket + many concurrent short connections producing tight bursts at bucket refill boundaries. If lots of cold containers fire at similar offsets you can push a single-minute bucket over the limit even if avg RPM < limit. Also check for retry loops missing jitter.

samir (devex): quick repro you can try locally to validate burst behavior:

```
for i in $(seq 1 250); do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete &
done
wait
```

Note: run without keep-alive to simulate many short TCP handshakes. To simulate keep-alive reuse, use a single long-lived HTTP connection or the SDK.

maria (sre): mitigation options:
- immediate: throttle the client side to spread requests across the minute (simple token-bucket client-side), add randomized jitter to retries.
- config: reduce client concurrency or enable connection pooling/keepalive so bursts are smoother.
- platform: we can enable "burst smoothing" for the account (server-side smoothing that redistributes small bursts) — request needed from support.
- long-term: move to Dedicated capacity if sustained bursty workload is business-critical.

jess (support): morphix-support — can you try enabling keepalive in the SDK and add a small randomized backoff on retries, and report results? I can open a platform request to enable burst smoothing if that helps.

morphix-support: will try the SDK keepalive + jitter this afternoon and report back. also we'll run the repro loop to confirm. thanks! :thumbsup:

samir (devex): if you need a quick patch, set a per-process concurrency cap (eg 10) in your SDK wrapper and add jittered exponential backoff (min 200ms, max 2s). I can share a snippet if useful.

jess (support): marking this thread for follow-up. escalate to account team if we still see >5% 429s after client changes. keeping ticket MORPH-915 open.
